title.desc: Ask in plain English. Deckhand asks for what it needs, runs the calculation, and sends back a report you can keep.

turns.html: Survey picked up a free span on one of our export lines and I want to know if it's a problem. Can you screen it for vortex-induced vibration?

Happy to screen it — a few details so I set it up right:
  • Pipe section — outer diameter, wall thickness, and steel grade?
  • What's the line carrying (content density), and its submerged weight on the seabed?
  • Measured span length and the seabed gap under the pipe?
  • The design current at pipe level, and the fatigue S-N class you work to?
This runs the DNV-RP-F105 free-span screen for a steel line on the seabed. A multi-span or a soil-interaction case needs the detailed method, so I'd flag that and pass it on.

10.75 inch line — OD 273.1 mm, wall 12.7 mm, X-grade steel. Carrying product at 900 kg/m³, submerged weight about 850 N/m. Surveyed span is 10 m with a 0.5 m gap to the seabed. Design current at the pipe is 0.8 m/s, and we screen to S-N curve F. Section's in the file.

Got it — single steel span on the seabed, so I'll run the screen directly. Basis I'll use: DNV-RP-F105 free-span screening — natural frequency from a pinned-pinned beam, reduced velocity against the in-line and cross-flow onset, and the allowable span back-calculated from the onset limit. Curve F for the fatigue check. Running it now…

Here's the screen — and it clears:
QuantityResultLimitVerdict
Natural frequency4.94 Hz——
Cross-flow VIV onset3.11 m/s current0.8 m/s design✅ No onset
Allowable span12.4 m10 m actual✅ Within
This span passes screening. The 0.8 m/s design current is below both the in-line (1.23 m/s) and cross-flow (3.11 m/s) VIV-onset currents, so VIV isn't triggered — no fatigue accumulation — and the 10 m span sits inside the 12.4 m allowable (81% utilisation).

report.title: Free-Span Screening (DNV-RP-F105)
report.inputs:
Pipe section
10.75 inch line · OD 273.1 mm · wall 12.7 mm · E = 207 GPa · steel 7,850 kg/m³
Content 900 kg/m³ · submerged weight 850 N/m

Span
Span length 10.0 m · seabed gap 0.5 m · pinned-pinned · no sag

Environment & design
current 0.8 m/s · seawater 1,025 kg/m³ · KC 30
S-N curve F (seawater, cathodic protection)
γ_IL 1.1 · γ_CF 1.3 · γ_k 1.15
report.methodology:
1 · Natural frequency from a pinned-pinned beam in still water, with added mass.
2 · Reduced velocity Ur = current ÷ (frequency × diameter).
3 · Compare Ur against the DNV-RP-F105 in-line and cross-flow onset values — VIV is active when Ur exceeds onset.
4 · Allowable span = the span at which Ur just reaches onset, back-calculated from the onset limit.
5 · Cross-flow stress range and fatigue life from the curve-F S-N relation; verdict screens span length and onset.

Verdict: PASS — VIV is not triggered at the design current (in-line and cross-flow onset both above 0.8 m/s), so no fatigue accumulation, and the 10 m span sits within the 12.4 m allowable.
